name: Pomegranate extract
summary: An ellagitannin-rich antioxidant extract with plenty of lab data and no confirmed skin-appearance results.
lead: Pomegranate extract is a concentrate of polyphenols obtained from the fruit, peel or seeds of Punica granatum, a tree native to the region spanning the Caucasus and the Iranian plateau . It is sold as an oral supplement and used in skincare as an antioxidant, with marketing built on its ellagitannin content.

name: Aloe leaf extract
summary: The classic soothing plant gel in after-sun and moisturizers; widely used, with conflicting evidence on wounds and little on appearance.
lead: Aloe leaf extract is a preparation from the leaves of Aloe vera, a succulent plant long used on the skin, with records of use dating to the fourth millennium BCE . In cosmetics it is a common soothing and moisturizing ingredient in lotions, gels, sunscreens, shampoos and facial products .

name: Sugarcane extract
summary: A plant source of glycolic acid pitched as a gentle natural exfoliant; the AHA is well known, the extract itself is untested for skin.
lead: Sugarcane extract refers to preparations from Saccharum officinarum used in cosmetics, most often described as a natural source of alpha hydroxy acids, chiefly glycolic acid. Glycolic acid can be isolated from sugarcane and is also found in sugar beets, pineapple, cantaloupe and unripe grapes .

name: Apple fruit water
summary: A mild fruit-acid botanical water in some creams; one formulation study and little else.
lead: Apple fruit water is a water-based extract of apple fruit used in cosmetics as a mild source of fruit acids and polyphenols. The sources reviewed contain a single dedicated study: a 2018 report on a cream containing 6 percent wild apple fruit water extract, said to contain 3.5 percent alpha hydroxy acids (AHAs) along with polyphenolic compounds, stabilized with biodegradable alkyl-polyglucoside emulsifiers .

name: Turmeric root extract
summary: Curcumin-rich plant extract sold as a skin brightener; evidence for that use is limited to cell studies.
lead: Turmeric root extract is a preparation made from the rhizome of Curcuma longa, a plant of the ginger family. Its main colored constituent is curcumin, a yellow polyphenol that is also used as a food coloring, a dietary supplement ingredient and a cosmetic ingredient. In skincare it is marketed mainly as a brightening or antioxidant ingredient.

name: Menthyl lactate
summary: Menthol-derived cooling ingredient used for feel in cosmetics; no evidence it changes appearance.
lead: Menthyl lactate is an ester of menthol and lactic acid used as a cooling agent, giving a milder and longer-lasting cooling sensation than menthol in product formulations described in patents. It appears in cosmetics, fragrances, oral-care and tobacco products.

name: Exosome serums
summary: Vesicle-based regeneration serums with promising biology but almost no published human skin data.
lead: Exosome serums are skincare and post-procedure products marketed as containing exosomes or other extracellular vesicles, small membrane-enclosed particles that cells release. They are promoted for regeneration and rejuvenation, often alongside procedures such as microneedling.

name: Mesenchymal stem cell conditioned media
summary: Stem-cell secretome liquid sold for regeneration; lab promise, only early-phase human trials.
lead: Mesenchymal stem cell conditioned media (MSC-CM), also called the MSC secretome, is the liquid in which mesenchymal stem cells have been grown, containing the proteins, growth factors, vesicles and other molecules they release. Versions made from adipose-derived stem cells (ADSC-CM) are among those studied. Products based on it are marketed in serums and post-procedure treatments for regeneration.

name: Fibroblast growth factor (FGF)
summary: Wound-healing growth factor put in anti-aging serums, with no human cosmetic trials found.
lead: Fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) are a family of 23 signaling proteins in humans that regulate cell growth, tissue organization and wound healing, signaling through four receptor types (FGFR1-4). FGF2, also called basic FGF (bFGF), promotes blood vessel formation, fibroblast proliferation and granulation tissue in wound repair. Topical FGF is included in some anti-aging serums.

name: Anagain
summary: Pea-sprout extract sold in cosmetic hair serums; backed by one tiny 10-person gene-expression study.
lead: Anagain (also written AnaGain) is a cosmetic hair-care ingredient derived from the sprouts of the pea plant, marketed in topical hair-growth serums and lotions. It is a branded cosmetic active rather than a drug, and it is discussed in appearance communities alongside other 'hair-growth actives' such as Redensyl, Capixyl and Baicapil.

name: Baicapil
summary: Baicalin-themed cosmetic hair active with no trial of its own found.
lead: Baicapil is a branded cosmetic hair-care active marketed for scalp hair-loss serums. Its name suggests a baicalin-based ingredient, and baicalin is a flavone glycoside found in Scutellaria (skullcap) species.

name: Dihydroquercetin glucoside
summary: A taxifolin derivative in Redensyl; no studies of it on its own.
lead: Dihydroquercetin glucoside (DHQG) is described in hair-care marketing as one of the two components of Redensyl, a cosmetic hair-growth active; the other is EGCG-glucoside. It is a glucoside of dihydroquercetin, also called taxifolin, a flavanonol found in Siberian larch, milk thistle and other plants.

name: EGCG-glucoside
summary: Green-tea catechin derivative used in Redensyl; no hair data on the component alone.
lead: EGCG-glucoside (EGCG2) is a glucosylated form of epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), the main catechin of green tea. In hair-care marketing it is named as one of the two components of Redensyl, alongside dihydroquercetin glucoside.

name: Biochanin A
summary: Red-clover isoflavone named in Capixyl; studied for other things, not hair.
lead: Biochanin A is an O-methylated isoflavone, a plant phytoestrogen found in red clover, soy, alfalfa sprouts, peanuts and chickpea. In hair-care marketing, red clover-derived biochanin A is named as a component of Capixyl, a cosmetic peptide-and-isoflavone hair-growth active.

name: Suvomipic
summary: Pelage's once-daily topical pyruvate-carrier inhibitor for hair loss, in phase 2 with early company-reported results.
lead: Suvomipic (developmental code PP405) is an experimental topical drug for hair loss developed by Pelage Pharmaceuticals, a company spun out of UCLA in 2018. It is described as a possible first-in-class compound that inhibits the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC1 and MPC2), which is thought to raise pyruvate and push hair follicle stem cells toward glycolysis and growth.

name: Quercitrin
summary: A plant flavonoid glycoside sometimes floated for hair, with antioxidant lab data but no hair studies in people.
lead: Quercitrin (quercetin 3-rhamnoside, also called thujin) is a flavonoid glycoside in which the flavonol quercetin is bound to the sugar rhamnose . It occurs in plants such as Tartary buckwheat and several oak species, and in the dye quercitron .

name: Horsetail extract
summary: A silica-rich herbal extract sold for hair and nails, with limited lab data and no single-ingredient hair trials.
lead: Horsetail extract is prepared from Equisetum arvense (field or common horsetail), a perennial non-flowering plant native to northern temperate regions . It is marketed in hair and nail supplements and shampoos as a source of silica, with the plant reported to contain silicon along with flavonoids, saponins, tannins and minerals .
claims: Horsetail silica strengthens hair and supports growth

name: Isoflavones
summary: Soy-derived phytoestrogens discussed for hair, but studied in people for other conditions, not hair.
lead: Isoflavones are plant compounds, concentrated in soybeans and other legumes, that act as phytoestrogens, meaning they have estrogen-like activity in mammals . The major soy isoflavones are genistein and daidzein, and daidzein can be converted by gut bacteria to equol .

name: Estrogen topical for hair
summary: Scalp estrogen solutions, mainly alfatradiol, that may slow thinning in some regions but are not shown to regrow hair.
lead: Topical estrogen for hair refers to estrogenic solutions applied to the scalp for pattern hair loss. The best-documented example is alfatradiol (17-alpha-estradiol), a weak estrogen and 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor sold as an ethanol-based scalp solution in Germany and some Latin American countries under names such as Ell-Cranell Alpha .

name: Triamcinolone injections
summary: A clinician-administered steroid injection for patchy alopecia areata, with reported regrowth in most treated patients.
lead: Triamcinolone acetonide is a synthetic glucocorticoid, about five times as potent as cortisol, sold under brand names such as Kenalog . Injected into the skin (intralesional), it is used for inflammatory skin conditions and keloid scars, and dermatologists also use it for patchy alopecia areata, an autoimmune hair-loss condition .
claims: Triamcinolone injections regrow patchy hair loss

name: Deuruxolitinib
summary: Newly approved oral JAK inhibitor for severe alopecia areata, with strong regrowth data and a boxed warning.
lead: Deuruxolitinib (brand name Leqselvi; formerly CTP-543) is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor approved in the United States for adults with severe alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition that causes patchy to total scalp and body hair loss. It is a deuterated form of a JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor, and in vitro assays reported in the US label showed greater inhibitory potency for JAK1, JAK2 and TYK2 than for JAK3.

name: Ruxolitinib oral
summary: Oral JAK inhibitor approved for blood and transplant disorders, only investigational for alopecia areata.
lead: Ruxolitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK1/JAK2) inhibitor developed by Incyte and sold orally as Jakafi in the United States and Jakavi elsewhere (Novartis). Its approved oral indications are blood and transplant conditions, namely myelofibrosis, polycythemia vera and graft-versus-host disease; a topical cream (Opzelura) is approved for atopic dermatitis and vitiligo.

name: Methotrexate for alopecia
summary: Old immunosuppressant tried off-label for alopecia areata, supported by small studies and a meta-analysis.
lead: Methotrexate is an immunosuppressant used in several skin diseases that has been tried off-label for alopecia areata, an autoimmune hair loss condition, either alone or alongside corticosteroids. A 2019 systematic review and meta-analysis described a paucity of definitive evidence and guidelines for this use.

name: Mometasone
summary: Potent steroid for allergies, asthma and eczema, with no hair-loss studies found.
lead: Mometasone furoate is a synthetic glucocorticoid used in nasal, inhaled and topical forms for allergic rhinitis, nasal polyps, asthma and inflammatory skin conditions such as eczema and psoriasis. Brand names include Nasonex, Asmanex and, for the topical form, Elocon.

name: Diaminopyrimidine oxide
summary: Minoxidil-like cosmetic ingredient in hair lotions, known mostly from patents and with no trials found.
lead: Diaminopyrimidine oxide is a minoxidil-related ingredient that appears in some hair-growth and anti-hair-loss lotions and shampoos. In the sources reviewed, it appears mainly in cosmetic patents, including Korean patent filings from 2007 and 2008 describing compositions of pyrrolidinyl diaminopyrimidine oxide for hair growth and for preventing hair loss.

name: Sarcosine (hair)
summary: A glycine-derived amino acid listed as a component in some hair-growth blends, with no hair studies behind it.
lead: Sarcosine, also called N-methylglycine, is a non-proteinogenic amino acid that is the N-methyl derivative of glycine. It occurs naturally in muscle and other tissues as an intermediate in the conversion of choline to glycine.

name: Cinnamomum zeylanicum bark extract
summary: Ceylon cinnamon bark extract, listed in a cosmetic blend, with no hair or scalp studies behind it.
lead: Cinnamomum zeylanicum is an older botanical name for Cinnamomum verum, the evergreen tree of Sri Lanka known as true or Ceylon cinnamon. Its dried inner bark is the cinnamon spice. Extracts of the bark are described as a component of Sepicontrol A5, a cosmetic ingredient blend.

name: Hydroxypropyl ammonium gluconate
summary: A gluconate humectant paired with a gluconamide in bond-building hair products; only crystal-chemistry research exists.
lead: 3-Hydroxypropyl ammonium gluconate is a gluconate salt used with a gluconamide derivative in a hair care mixture that is described as strengthening hair fibres. A 2022 crystallography paper states that the mechanism of that mixture on hair was unknown and examined how the gluconamide and gluconate interact with amino acids.

name: Hydrolyzed silk protein
summary: Broken-down silk protein used as a conditioning ingredient; no hair trials found.
lead: Hydrolyzed silk protein is silk protein broken into smaller peptides and amino acids, used in cosmetic products including hair conditioners. Silk is mainly fibroin with a coating of sericin.

name: Hydrolyzed keratin
summary: Broken-down keratin protein added to conditioners; marketed for repair, with almost no hair-specific human data.
lead: Hydrolyzed keratin is keratin, the structural protein of hair, wool, nails and feathers, that has been broken down into smaller peptide and amino-acid fragments so that it can dissolve in water. It is used as a protein ingredient in hair conditioners and similar products, where it is marketed for strengthening and repairing damaged hair.
